Definition: from G1410; a ruler or officer:--of great authority, mighty, potentate.
BiblicalUsage: A ruler, a mighty one, as the Ethiopian eunuch was a man of great authority under Candace, and Mary sang that God has put down the mighty from their seats. Paul calls Christ the only Potentate, the King of kings and Lord of lords, who alone has immortality.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe every potentate on earth is a small shadow of the one Potentate, and the mighty are put down so the lowly can be lifted. Christ alone holds immortality, and I bow to Him, not to them.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
